title: Energy in a swinging or rolling system
log: 2026-11-04T09:36:58Z write: the API refused it in the chapter request, so it is written on its own next

draft.title: Energy in a swinging or rolling system
card: The higher an object is above the ground, the more gravitational potential energy it has. The faster it moves, the more kinetic energy it has.
On a roller-coaster, the cars slow down as they climb. Kinetic energy is transformed into gravitational potential energy.
As the cars drop, height falls and speed rises. Gravitational potential energy is transformed into kinetic energy.

A pendulum does the same. It is fastest at the lowest point, where kinetic energy is greatest. It is highest at the end of each swing, where it stops for a moment and gravitational potential energy is greatest.
draft.remember: As height goes up, speed goes down, and the energy changes back and forth between the two forms.

a.q: A swing is at the top of its arc and is stopped for an instant. Which energy does it have the most of at that point?
a.why: At the top of the arc the swing is at its highest point, so gravitational potential energy is greatest. Kinetic energy is greatest at the bottom, where the swing moves fastest, so it is not the answer here.
a.clue: Think about height at the top of the arc.

b.q: A roller-coaster car rolls down a long slope from the top of a hill. What happens to its energy as it drops?
opts: Potential energy falls and kinetic energy rises
Potential energy rises and kinetic energy falls
Both potential and kinetic energy rise
Both potential and kinetic energy fall
b.why: As the car drops, its height falls, so gravitational potential energy falls. Its speed rises, so kinetic energy rises. Climbing a hill would be the reverse, which is the tempting wrong option.
b.clue: Check what happens to height and to speed as the car drops.

b.best: Potential energy falls and kinetic energy rises
